# 0006 — Storage abstraction

**Context.** Photos are large and numerous; databases are a poor blob store; production will use S3 or Azure Blob.

**Decision.** `IStorageService` (save, open, delete, exists, `GetReadUrlAsync`, `CreateDirectUploadAsync`). The MVP implementation is local disk: write-once objects, keys generated by the server (`inspections/{id}/rooms/{id}/{mediaId}.jpg`, no user input), and **signed, expiring URLs** (`/api/files/...?exp&sig`, HMAC-SHA256) — the local equivalent of presigned URLs. URLs are only issued after the API has authorized the caller for that inspection/report. `InspectionRoomMedia` stores metadata only (type, size, SHA-256, uploader, status).

Uploads go through the API today and are validated by content (magic bytes: JPEG/PNG/WebP), size and ownership. `MediaStatus.Pending` and `CreateDirectUploadAsync` exist so direct-to-bucket uploads can be added without touching the domain: issue a ticket → client uploads → client confirms → media becomes `Ready`. Finalization already refuses pending uploads.

**Consequences.** Adding S3/Blob = one new class + configuration. Local storage is single-node only (use a shared volume or object storage when scaling out).
